title: Book One · Chapter 2: One Small Box
story:
At home, Mum gives Ronan a small box.

"This one is for your things."

Ronan puts it on the floor.

"Do all my things go in this box?"

"Your clothes go in a bag. Your blanket goes with the beds. What else do you want to keep? Put those things in this box."

Ronan looks around the room.

He wants to keep the room.

There is a tree outside the window. In the morning, its shadow falls across his bed. Sometimes he puts his feet in the shadow. Sometimes he puts them in the sun.

"Is there a tree at the new home?" he asks.

"There is a yard," Mum says.

"Is there a tree in that yard?"

"You can look tomorrow."

Ronan takes his book from under the bed. There is a boat on the front. The boat has a red sail.

He puts the book in the box.

Next, he finds his little wooden boat. Dad made it. One end is green. The other end is still just wood.

"You can finish it one day," Dad says from the door.

He has his blue box in one hand.

"Can I finish it at the new home?" Ronan asks.

"Yes."

Ronan puts the boat beside the book.

Then he takes the bell from his pocket.

He presses it once.

Mum looks up.

"Is that the dinner bell?"

"No. It's my bike bell."

"Then I will call you myself."

She calls his name very loudly. Ronan puts his hands over his ears.

"I'm right here!"

"Good," Mum says. "It works."

Ronan almost smiles.

He puts the bell between the boat and the book. Then he moves it again. The wood can scratch the bell. He moves the bell away from the boat.

Dad sits on the floor. He folds a shirt and puts it in a bag.

Ronan watches him.

"Will you sell the boat?"

Dad stops folding.

"No."

"Will you sell the bell, too?"

"No."

"Please ask me first."

Dad puts the shirt down.

"Yes," he says. "I will ask you first."

Ronan looks at Dad for a moment. Then he moves the box closer to his bed.

Mum brings him a piece of paper.

"You can draw our old room," she says. "Then you can take the picture with you."

Ronan finds a pencil.

He draws the window first. He draws the tree outside it. His tree has a thick middle. Its thin branches look like arms.

"It looks like Dad," he says.

Dad looks at the picture.

"I need more leaves."

Ronan gives the tree two big leaves at the top.

"Now you have hair."

Mum laughs. Dad touches the top of his head.

Ronan draws Mum beside the tree. He draws himself by the window.

He looks at the picture. There is no bike in it.

His pencil stays above the paper.

Then he draws the bike under the tree.

"That one can stay," he says.

He puts the picture in the box. Mum helps him close it.

"There's a little space left," she says.

Ronan looks at the empty corner.

"I can put something from the new home there."

He carries the box to the door and puts it beside Dad's blue one.
studyGuide:
## 先看情节提示也可以

Ronan 把书、木船和车铃放进箱子，并画下旧房间；他要求爸爸先问自己再动这些东西。

## 从认词到读句子

1. **The boat / has / a red sail.** 船／有／一面红帆。
2. **Ronan / puts the boat / beside the book.** Ronan／把木船放下／放在书旁。

画树的笑话：arms在这里把树枝说成手臂；Dad把两片叶子当作自己的头发。不是说树真的变成了爸爸。

---

## 重点词句

| 表达 | 本章意思 |
|---|---|
| fold | 折叠；这里是叠衣服 |
| finish | 做完、完成 |
| space | 空间、空位 |
| scratch | 刮花、划伤 |

旧词复现：box、keep、bell、pocket、put … down、hand、home。

辅助理解：shadow＝影子；yard＝院子；sail＝船帆；leaf / leaves＝叶子。

"Then you can take the picture with you."＝"这样你就可以把它带在身边。"the picture 指他画下来的旧房间。

## 理解与回访

1. Ronan 把哪些东西放进自己的箱子？
2. 他向 Dad 提出了什么要求？Dad 怎样回应？

换个场景看旧词：*Please keep this message.* 这里的 keep 仍然表示"保留"。
